outcome: neonatal morbidity (prematurity, sepsis, Intra-uterine growth restriction (IUGR), perinatal asphyxia)
neonatal mortality (intrauterine death, stillbirths, early neonatal deaths)
cohort: 75 eclamptic mothers and their 76 babies (74 singletons, 1 set of twins) delivered in Darbhanga, Bihar, India.
finding: Eclampsia remains a significant risk factor for adverse neonatal morbidities (preterm birth, LBW, IUGR, birth asphyxia) and mortality, with young maternal age, nulliparity, and vaginal mode of delivery also contributing to adverse perinatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Vaginal mode of delivery was identified as a risk factor for adverse perinatal outcomes in babies born to eclamptic mothers, while Caesarean delivery was the commonest mode.
